policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv אשדודיות and qere אַשְׁדֳּדִיּוֹת differ only in orthography (plene vs. defective spelling of the same gentilic plural); ASV 'women of Ashdod' renders either identically. The only note on the verse is a hebrew_gloss on 'had married', not mapped to this unit. Base qere fallback retained.

Ketiv עמוניות and qere עַמֳּנִיּוֹת differ only in orthography (plene vs. defective spelling of the same gentilic plural); ASV 'of Ammon' renders either identically. The only note on the verse is a hebrew_gloss on 'had married', not mapped to this unit. Base qere fallback retained.
